meta.name: Obsidian Sentinel
meta.description: A precision command-console system for enterprise SOC/SIEM platforms — dense, fast to scan, unmistakably serious.
meta.personality: Obsidian Sentinel reads like a hardened operations console, not a consumer app skinned dark. Near-black graphite surfaces, a cold radar-teal for interactive elements, a dedicated five-step severity ramp for triage at a glance, and IBM Plex's mono/sans pairing so log lines, hashes, and IPs render with the same technical precision as the UI chrome around them. Sharp small-radius geometry throughout — nothing bubbly, nothing playful.

primary.usage: Primary buttons, active nav item, key interactive elements, focus rings, links

primary-hover.usage: Hover/active state for primary-colored elements (darkens, does not lighten)

secondary.usage: Secondary buttons, inactive tabs, neutral interactive chrome

accent.usage: Notification dots, highlighted metrics, 'new'/'updated' badges, warm counterpoint to primary teal

surface-elevated.usage: Modals, dropdowns, popovers, toasts — one step brighter than surface

border.usage: Default dividers, card borders, input borders, table row separators

border-strong.usage: Hover borders, focused inputs, emphasized dividers

text-primary.usage: Body copy, headings, primary data values (soft white-blue, not pure white, for long-shift eye comfort)

text-secondary.usage: Labels, captions, table headers, secondary metadata

text-muted.usage: Placeholders, disabled text, timestamps, low-emphasis helper text

text-on-primary.usage: Text/icons sitting on top of primary-teal-colored backgrounds

success.usage: Healthy/online/resolved states, success toasts, up-trend indicators

warning.usage: Degraded states, pending-review flags, caution toasts

error.usage: Failed actions, destructive-action confirmation, error toasts

critical.usage: Critical severity badge/row accent — same hue family as error, reserved for the top of the triage stack

informational.usage: Info-level severity badge/row accent — deliberately desaturated so it recedes under real findings

font-mono.usage: IPs, hashes, hostnames, timestamps, log/event payloads, rule IDs, code, terminal output — anything the analyst needs to read character-by-character

sm.usage: Table cells, form labels, secondary UI text — the default density for a data-heavy SOC console
Inputs, small chips, subtle lift off the surface

glow.usage: Focus ring / active-selection glow using primary teal

input.font: font-mono (for value fields like IP/search), font-body (for free text)

badge.pattern: 10% opacity tint of the semantic color as background, full-strength semantic color as text and 30% opacity border of the same color
